newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Elders sees flat 96/97 profit outlook.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Elders sees flat 96/97 profit outlook.

text.p: Pastoral group Elders Australia Ltd said the outlook for wool and cattle prices remains poor, making an expected flat profit result for the year to June 30, 1997.
Elders earlier reported a 3.3 percent decline in net profit to A$14.05 million for 1995/96.
"Wool and cattle prices remain poor, particularly in comparsion to average prices experienced during the same period last year," Elders said in a statement accompanying its 1995/96 annual results.

"This business is being managed against this background and management have planned for the new financial year on the basis of little or no significant increase in wool and cattle returns," Elders said.
"The 1996/97 profit outlook for Elders is therefore, relatively flat," it said. Elders also announced it would not pay a final dividend, compared with four cents a year earlier.
Elders is subject to a scrip and cash offer from Futuris Corp Ltd, which now owns 49 percent of the rural group.
Futuris is offering 10 of its shares for every nine Elders shares plus 23 cents per Elders share.
It said Elders Wool increased its market share by 1.6 percent over the previous year, but the price of the average bale of wool decreased by 20 percent.

Difficult trading conditions were experienced by Elders Wool International during the period, caused by lower production levels, subdued overseas demand and the rapid decline in the market price, it said.

Elders Livestock achieved an increase in market share, but cattle prices declined sharply in the second half of 1995/96 due to oversupply of cattle from the U.S. and instability in overseas beef markets arising from health issues, Elders said.
Elders said the live cattle export business continued its excellent performance with a record 124,000 head of cattle exported in 1995/96 compared with 121,000 head in 1994/95.
Elders shares closed two cents up at A$1.78.
